excerpt: A Formal C17 Compiler in ARM64 Assembly that cross-compiles to x86-64. A Literate Program. - LiterateDrivenDevelopment/kcc
content_html:
kcc is a formal C17 compiler written entirely in ARM64 assembly, and set down as a single literate program using weft, a metalanguage built to be authored and read by human and AI collaborators alike. Every instruction is explained in prose before it is written in code.

It checks C against the Standard, optimises it, allocates registers, and emits native machine code; it compiles itself to a byte-identical binary; and it cross-compiles to x86-64 (Linux and macOS). It builds and runs Lua, SQLite, and DOOM — and boots a Linux kernel.

The whole book is the compiler (≈1000 pages): read kcc.pdf in this repository, also published on Releases, or build it yourself (see below). Learn more about Literate Driven Development at https://literatedriven.com.

The .weft files are the only source of truth

Everything the machine builds — the assembly modules, the verification scripts, and the Makefile itself — is generated by tangling the literate sources. You never edit generated files; you edit the book.

kcc.weft          master document (LaTeX preamble + @i includes)
literate/         all the chapters (prose + code fragments)
assets/           cover art (SVG → the PDF covers)
kcc.pdf           the typeset book (committed; rebuilt with `make pdf`)
README.md         this file
LICENSE           MIT

The typeset book, kcc.pdf, is committed, so the repository always carries a readable copy of the current text. Rebuild it with make pdf.

Build

There is a one-time bootstrap: because the Makefile is itself tangled from the book, you generate it first, then use it.

# 1. Tangle sources, scripts, and the Makefile into gen/ (and ./Makefile).
weft -p gen/ --mkdirs kcc.weft

# 2. Build the compiler (gen/kcc).
make

# 3. Compile something with it.
./gen/kcc gen/hello.c -o gen/hello && ./gen/hello

-p gen/ prepends gen/ to every tangle output; --mkdirs creates the directories. The generated tree lives entirely under gen/ (plus the root Makefile); make clean removes it and the command above regenerates it.

Common targets

Target What it does
make / make build assemble + link gen/kcc
make difftest compile a corpus with kcc and clang, compare
make diagtest / make warntest invalid programs are rejected; -Wall warns
make test-codegen / make e2e / make interop run generated programs
make selfhost-* recompile a module in C with kcc, relink, verify
make meta-c full self-host fixpoint on Linux (needs Docker + qemu)
make ci the complete verification suite
make pdf weave the book and typeset kcc.pdf

The verification scripts locate their own base directory, so they work under any -p prefix.

The book

make pdf weaves the .weft sources to kcc.tex and typesets kcc.pdf with LuaLaTeX. The covers are regenerated from assets/*.svg when rsvg-convert is available. The resulting kcc.pdf is committed alongside the sources, so the book can be read straight from the repository; tagged versions are also published as a Release asset on GitLab.

Prerequisites

  • weft ≥2.0.0 (the literate tool).
  • A C toolchain's as and ld (Xcode command-line tools on macOS).
  • For the book: a TeX distribution with LuaLaTeX and latexmk — a full TeX Live, or the lightweight TinyTeX (a minimal TeX Live) — and, optionally, rsvg-convert for the covers.
  • For make meta-c and the kernel-boot reproduction: Docker and qemu-user.

License
